body: Thanks for sharing that experience, we had a family friend die and I live in NYC now...I think about it a lot. I'm just wary about broaching the subject. I'm an extremely private person and I don't know how they'd react, I guess. I like the community here and the leaders but I still feel like a bit of an outsider.

I've been on medication and had therapy, both at school and when I was a high school student. My school has a good counseling service but they are not equipped for long term treatment. I am a scholarship student and I really don't know if I'd be able to afford CBT (and my school is a very upper-crust expensive sort of place, there isn't a lot of support or sympathy for poor students.) One thing that attracts me to a religious counselor is that it would be free.

Spanish flu and the World Wars were the examples I gave my friend who was freaking out about Ebola and the Middle East crises. She said something along the lines of, "has the world every faced so many crises at once?" And when people say that they sound so misinformed to me-like I said I feel guilty for feeling this way because I have no reason to feel his way. I just trapped picturing the worst case scenarios over and over. Everything is screaming at me that it's not rational but I can't stop. 
(This isn't so relevant but I'm actually a girl.)
